cases.rationale: Current-era chart-only example with explicit 10-second micro and first-new-high language, without a hidden-buyer justification for the first trade.
Explicit first micro pullback trade with reported fills and a profitable first campaign.
Same-day recap explicitly identifies a 10-second first-candle-new-high entry and later describes another pullback as picture perfect.
Explicit 10-second micro pullback entry near $2.40 followed by continuation through $3.

The full timestamped source transcript proves that the approximately $5.25 ten-second micro, topping-tail rejection and loss belong to the earlier NCO/ONCO discussion, not ARTL. Ross reports the first ARTL trade separately at approximately $6.34, but the chart timeframe and pullback ordinal are unresolved. ARTL is retained only as catalyst/discretion evidence and must not contribute to Micro scoring.

Micro v0.1 can be judged on detecting/participating in the pullback family and ordinal, but the human $6 continuation trigger and ~$6.30 fill require context not present in the canonical chart-only baseline.
Narration explicitly attributes anticipation to stacked buyers and green time-and-sales, which Micro v0.1 deliberately excludes.

Useful for upstream selection and execution/no-fill research; its reported ~64M share figure also puts it outside the current low-float baseline. The transcript-derived YOLO label was corrected to YOUL only after a separate retrospective market-wide identity audit.
Preserves front-side versus back-side and heavy-seller context without forcing several different setup families into one Micro v0.1 score.
The recap itself says the skipped first micro could have or maybe should have been taken, so treating the skip as ground-truth correctness would overstate the evidence.
